clue.text: Fire a number on standard allowance

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written
a standard is a flag or banner
a ration is a fixed allowance of food

explanation.surface: A fire chief is put on a standard allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflagration is a great, destructive blaze.

clue.text: You see, but you do not remarked Sherlock Holmes

definitions.text: You see, but you do not remarked Sherlock Holmes

parts.words: You see, but you do not remarked Sherlock Holmes
parts.note: a fill-in quotation: the missing verb completes the detective's famous rebuke to Watson in A Scandal in Bohemia

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes chides Watson for seeing without truly noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is 'You see, but you do not observe', so the answer is the word the clue leaves out.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation contrasts merely seeing with watching closely, which is what the missing verb means.

clue.text: Just for fun!

definitions.meaning: a funfair is a travelling show of rides and stalls, shortened to one word

explanation.definitionFit: The word means equitable, and is also a fête or carnival of amusements.

clue.text: Making sure tea is quite plain

indicators.note: making something of the letters means building a new word from them, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Brewing up properly yields a very plain cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' signals the anagram: SURE TEA rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something severe and unadorned is very plain.

clue.text: Regard for a certain feature

definitions.meaning: regard here means esteem or admiration
as in 'in one ...', a particular point or detail

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both esteem and a particular point or aspect of something.

clue.text: The inexperienced man may have to hold up transport

indicators.note: the word 'to' grips the next piece between its two letters, so it acts as a container

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a form of transport

explanation.surface: A novice might hold up the traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' looks like a phrase for delaying traffic; here 'to hold' makes the word 'to' a container and 'up' turns the railway abbreviation upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a beginner or novice.

clue.text: Gets boats in for repair

indicators.note: putting something in for repair means it is taken apart and reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone collects vessels that were sent to the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain is to acquire or get hold of.

clue.text: Minor missile occasioning little discord

parts.note: minor means slight or unimportant
a quarrel is a square-headed bolt shot from a crossbow

explanation.surface: A small projectile sparks a tiff.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor disagreement is a little discord between people.

clue.text: He'll arrange for others to take steps

definitions.text: He'll arrange for others to take steps

parts.words: He'll arrange for others to take steps
parts.note: reads like an organiser delegating action, but the steps are dance steps someone sets out for performers

explanation.surface: A manager delegates action to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance designer plans the moves that performers carry out.

clue.text: Girls' stretching of the truth about dope

definitions.note: the plural answer stands for girls; the possessive apostrophe is surface dressing

indicators.note: lies are wrapped about the next piece, so they form the container

parts.note: stretching the truth means telling lies
a dope is a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: Young women exaggerate about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: LIES goes 'about' ASS, giving L(ASS)IES. LASSIES is Scottish and northern English for girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasses are young women, a regional word for girls.

clue.text: Score, not being handicapped

definitions.meaning: to score is to scrape or mark a surface
a ... player in golf or racing receives no handicap

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a scraped mark, and also describes a competitor given no head start or allowance.

clue.text: Grit may well be called for when so circumscribed

indicators.note: the letters are being called on for a fresh arrangement here, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Courage is needed when you are hemmed in.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GRIT, rearranged, give a word for encircled. 'when so' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Girt is an old past participle of gird, meaning encircled or surrounded.

clue.text: Several will appear in this evening's TV

indicators.note: the answer will appear inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A listing promises a number of shows on tonight's television.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'thiS EVENing's'. Several is loose for a definite number, but stands for 'a handful'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small number like this one is a handful, which several suggests.

clue.text: Row about it in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived for about, concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dispute about something that happened after someone stopped work.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + IT gives REIT, which 'in retirement' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a set of rows rising one above another.

clue.text: Strong drink

definitions.meaning: a dark beer such as porter

explanation.definitionFit: The word means sturdy and robust, and is also a dark, heavy beer.

clue.text: At the side of a supporter

parts.note: a beam is a timber that supports a structure

explanation.surface: Someone stands beside a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, abeam means level with the side, at right angles to the keel.

clue.text: Where entertainment is provided at three maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A show is staged at three o'clock, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is the venue where plays and shows are staged.

clue.text: Thanks to well-qualified people, business is really hot!

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates
CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: Thanks to the experts, trade is booming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'really hot' describes the fiery chilli sauce, not booming trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The pepper sauce is famously fiery, so the clue calls it very spicy.

clue.text: Set out in a Continental church without any formality

parts.note: un is French for a, so a Continental 'a'

indicators.note: one piece is set inside another, placing it within
in places the word out within the abbreviation for church

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something laid out in a European church lacks ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking polish and manners means behaving with no formality or refinement.

clue.text: The sculptor has little room in one

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An artist works in a tiny studio.
explanation.walkthrough: Benvenuto Cellini was a Florentine Renaissance sculptor and goldsmith.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellini was an Italian Renaissance artist famed for his bronze Perseus.

clue.text: To rouse a woman is a bloomer!

parts.note: to heat is to excite or inflame
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Getting a woman worked up is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering moorland shrub is something that blooms.

clue.text: Kitchen gadget-when working rotates

indicators.note: working means set in motion and reorganised, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A kitchen appliance turns round as it operates.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an electric appliance for browning bread.

clue.text: Matron's moved across the light

indicators.note: moved means shifted about, so the letters change places

parts.note: the letters of matron plus S

explanation.surface: A hospital matron has been relocated across from the window.
explanation.walkthrough: A transom is a crossbar above a door or across a window, the 'light' being the glazed opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal crossbar spans a window or the glazing above a door.

clue.text: Call egghead about it, being a sociable creature

indicators.note: the first pieces go about the word it, holding it inside

parts.note: to term is to name or call
the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: Someone calls a brainy person friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM and E go 'about' IT: TERM(IT)E. Termites live in large, organised colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are social insects living in large colonies.

clue.text: Wind register

definitions.meaning: to wind is to ... up, as yarn
a ... is a list of names, as in a ... call

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to coil up and also an official list of names.

clue.text: Reject almost everything that's commonplace

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit or reject

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Turn down nearly everything ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final L from ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trite and unoriginal is ordinary and commonplace.

clue.text: A word of advice about the right excursion

indicators.note: the tip goes round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint

explanation.surface: A suggestion about the correct outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey or outing.

clue.text: Fixed in haste

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Fixed in haste' (4) for PAST: no parse gives PAST; the wordplay suggests POST (fixed, and post-haste), so the clue or answer is misread

clue.text: Remains, as some effort seems desirable

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their letters are taken

explanation.surface: Leftovers, it seems some effort is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'effORT Seems'. Orts are scraps of leftover food.
explanation.definitionFit: Orts are scraps or leftovers from a meal.

clue.text: Grave words

parts.note: reads as serious speech, but the words are carved on a tombstone

explanation.surface: Solemn remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tomb is literally text at a burial place.

clue.text: Ceremony involving a tree

definitions.meaning: a religious rite or formal occasion
the ... tree is a European tree related to the rowan

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a religious rite and also a European tree of the rose family.

clue.text: A coach of times gone by

definitions.text: A coach of times gone by

parts.words: A coach of times gone by
parts.note: reads as an old stagecoach, but means a teacher whose subject is the past

explanation.surface: An antique horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolteacher whose subject is the past tutors pupils in bygone times.
